**Dallas**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-11) is a city in the U.S. state of [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"). Located in [northern Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas "North Texas"), it is the [ninth-most populous city in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population") and [third-most populous city in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Texas_by_population "List of cities in Texas by population"), with a population of 1.3 million at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Infoplease-2023-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-13) Along with the city of [Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas "Fort Worth, Texas"), Dallas anchors the [Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex"), the [fourth-most populous metropolitan area in the U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_statistical_area "Metropolitan statistical area") and the [most populous metropolitan area in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Texas_metropolitan_areas "List of Texas metropolitan areas"), at 8.5 million people.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-14) Dallas is a core city of the largest metropolitan area in the [Southern U.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States") and the largest inland metropolitan area in the U.S. that lacks any navigable link to the sea.[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-15) It is the [seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Dallas County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_County,_Texas "Dallas County, Texas"), covering nearly 386 square miles (1,000 km 2) and extending into [Collin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collin_County,_Texas "Collin County, Texas"), [Denton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denton_County,_Texas "Denton County, Texas"), [Kaufman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaufman_County,_Texas "Kaufman County, Texas"), and [Rockwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwall_County,_Texas "Rockwall County, Texas") counties.

Both Dallas and Fort Worth were initially developed as a product of the construction of major railroad lines through the area allowing access to cotton, cattle, and later oil in North and [East Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Texas "East Texas"). The construction of the [Interstate Highway System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_Highway_System "Interstate Highway System") reinforced Dallas's prominence as a transportation hub, with four major interstate highways converging in the city and a fifth interstate loop around it. Dallas then developed as a strong industrial and financial center and a major inland port, due to the convergence of major railroad lines, interstate highways, and the construction of [Dallas Fort Worth International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Fort_Worth_International_Airport "Dallas Fort Worth International Airport"), one of the largest and [busiest airports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_busiest_airports_by_passenger_traffic "List of busiest airports by passenger traffic") in the world.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-handbook_dallas2-16) In addition, [Dallas Area Rapid Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Area_Rapid_Transit "Dallas Area Rapid Transit") (DART) operates rail and bus transit services throughout the city and its surrounding suburbs.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-17)

Dominant sectors of its diverse economy include defense, financial services (such as traditional banking, investment banking, private equity, and venture capital), information technology, telecommunications, and [transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transportation_in_Dallas "Transportation in Dallas"). The Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex hosts 23 [_Fortune_ 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") companies, the second-most in Texas and fourth-most in the United States,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-ODOnnell-2022-18)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Fortune-2022a-19) and 11 of those companies are located within Dallas city limits.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Fortune-2022-20)[Over 41 colleges and universities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_colleges_and_universities_in_the_Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "List of colleges and universities in the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex") are located within its metropolitan area, which is the most of any metropolitan area in Texas. The city has a population from a myriad of ethnic and religious backgrounds.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [History of Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Dallas "History of Dallas")

For a chronological guide, see [Timeline of Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeline_of_Dallas "Timeline of Dallas").

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Cram_Dallas%2C_Texas_1890_UTA.jpg/250px-Cram_Dallas%2C_Texas_1890_UTA.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Cram_Dallas,_Texas_1890_UTA.jpg)

George C. Cram's 1890 map of Dallas

Indigenous tribes in [North Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas "North Texas") included the [Caddo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caddo "Caddo"), [Tawakoni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tawakoni "Tawakoni"), [Wichita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wichita_people "Wichita people"), [Kickapoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kickapoo "Kickapoo") and [Comanche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comanche "Comanche").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-23) Spanish colonists claimed the territory of Texas in the 18th century as a part of the Viceroyalty of [New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Spain "New Spain"). Later, France also [claimed the area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_colonial_empire "French colonial empire") but never established much settlement. In all, six flags have flown over the area preceding and during the city's history: those of France, Spain, and Mexico, the flag of the Republic of Texas, the Confederate flag, and the flag of the United States of America.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-24)

In 1819, the [Adams–Onís Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams%E2%80%93On%C3%ADs_Treaty "Adams–Onís Treaty") between the United States and Spain defined the [Red River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_River_of_the_South "Red River of the South") as the northern boundary of New Spain, officially placing the future location of Dallas well within Spanish territory.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-bolton-25)[_[page needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] The area remained under Spanish rule until 1821, when [Mexico declared independence from Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_War_of_Independence "Mexican War of Independence"), and the area was considered part of the Mexican state of [Coahuila y Tejas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coahuila_y_Tejas "Coahuila y Tejas"). In 1836, [Texians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texians "Texians"), with a majority of [Anglo-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglo-Americans "Anglo-Americans") settlers, [gained independence from Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Revolution "Texas Revolution") and formed the [Republic of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Texas "Republic of Texas").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-handbook_republic_of_texas-26)

Three years after Texas achieved independence, [John Neely Bryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Neely_Bryan "John Neely Bryan") surveyed the area around present-day Dallas.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-27) In 1839, accompanied by his dog and a Cherokee he called Ned, he planted a stake in the ground on a bluff located near three forks of the Trinity River and left.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-28) Two years later, in 1841, he returned to establish a permanent settlement named Dallas.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-29) The [origin of the name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Dallas_(1839%E2%80%931855)#Establishment "History of Dallas (1839–1855)") is uncertain. The official historical marker states it was named after Vice President [George M. Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_M._Dallas "George M. Dallas") of [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"). However, this is disputed. Other potential theories for the origin include his brother, [Commodore Alexander James Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_J._Dallas_(United_States_Navy_officer) "Alexander J. Dallas (United States Navy officer)"), as well as brothers Walter R. Dallas and James R. Dallas.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-30)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-31) A further theory gives the ultimate origin as the village of [Dallas, Moray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas,_Moray "Dallas, Moray"), Scotland,[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-32) similar to the way [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"), Texas, was named after [Sam Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Houston "Sam Houston"), whose ancestors came from the Scottish village of [Houston, Renfrewshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston,_Renfrewshire "Houston, Renfrewshire").

The Republic of Texas was [annexed by the United States in 1845](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_annexation "Texas annexation") and Dallas County was established the following year. Dallas was formally incorporated as a city on February 2, 1856.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-handbook_dallas2-16) In the mid-1800s, a group of French Socialists established [La Réunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_R%C3%A9union_(Dallas) "La Réunion (Dallas)"), a short-lived community, along the Trinity River in what is now West Dallas.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-33)

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/62/Postcard_of_crowd_two_hours_after_the_lynching_of_Allen_Brooks_in_1910.jpg/250px-Postcard_of_crowd_two_hours_after_the_lynching_of_Allen_Brooks_in_1910.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Postcard_of_crowd_two_hours_after_the_lynching_of_Allen_Brooks_in_1910.jpg)

A postcard of the [lynching of Allen Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching_of_Allen_Brooks "Lynching of Allen Brooks") in [Downtown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dallas "Downtown Dallas"), 1910

With the construction of railroads, Dallas became a business and trading center and was booming by the end of the 19th century. It became an industrial city, attracting workers from [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas"), the South, and the [Midwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midwestern_United_States "Midwestern United States"). The [Praetorian Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Praetorian_Building "Praetorian Building") in Dallas of 15 stories, built in 1909, was among the first [skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscrapers "Skyscrapers") west of [the Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River") and the tallest building in Texas for some time.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-34) It marked the prominence of Dallas as a city. A racetrack for [thoroughbreds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoroughbred "Thoroughbred") was built and their owners established the Dallas Jockey Club. Trotters raced at a track in Fort Worth, where a similar drivers club was based. The rapid expansion of population increased competition for jobs and housing.

In 1910, a white mob of hundreds of people [lynched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching "Lynching") a black man, [Allen Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynching_of_Allen_Brooks "Lynching of Allen Brooks"), accused of raping a little girl. The mob tortured Brooks, then killed him at the downtown [intersection of Main and Akard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Street_District,_Dallas "Main Street District, Dallas") by [hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanging "Hanging") him from a decorative archway inscribed with the words "Welcome Visitors". Thousands of Dallasites came to gawk at the torture scene, collecting keepsakes and posing for photographs.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Minutaglio-35)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-36)

In 1921, the Mexican president [Álvaro Obregón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Obreg%C3%B3n "Álvaro Obregón") along with the former revolutionary general visited Downtown Dallas's Mexican Park in [Little Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Mexico "Little Mexico"); the small park was on the corner of Akard and Caruth Street, site of the current Fairmont Hotel.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-37) The small neighborhood of Little Mexico was home to a Latin American population that had been drawn to Dallas by factors including the [American Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Dream "American Dream"), better living conditions,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-38) and the Mexican Revolution.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-39) Despite the onset of the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression"), business in construction was flourishing in 1930. That year, [Columbus Marion "Dad" Joiner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus_Marion_%22Dad%22_Joiner "Columbus Marion \"Dad\" Joiner") struck oil 100 miles (160 km) east of Dallas in [Kilgore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilgore,_Texas "Kilgore, Texas"), spawning the East [Texas oil boom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Oil_Boom "Texas Oil Boom"). Dallas quickly became the financial center for the oil industry in Texas and [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-historicalsociety-40)

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), Dallas was a major manufacturing center for military automobiles and aircraft for the United States and Allied forces. Over 94,000 jeeps and over 6,000 military trucks were produced at the Ford plant in East Dallas.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-41) North American Aviation manufactured over 18,000 aircraft at their plant in Dallas, including the [T-6 Texan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_T-6_Texan "North American T-6 Texan") trainer, [P-51 Mustang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_P-51_Mustang "North American P-51 Mustang") fighter, and [B-24 Liberator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consolidated_B-24_Liberator "Consolidated B-24 Liberator") bomber.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-42)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/59/JFK_Motorcade_GettyImages-517330536.jpg/250px-JFK_Motorcade_GettyImages-517330536.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JFK_Motorcade_GettyImages-517330536.jpg)

President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") riding in a [convertible car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convertible "Convertible") outside of Dallas, along with his wife, [Jacqueline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Kennedy "Jackie Kennedy"), and others inside, minutes before [he was assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy "Assassination of John F. Kennedy").

On November 22, 1963, [United States President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")[John F. Kennedy was assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy "Assassination of John F. Kennedy") on Elm Street while his [motorcade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidential_state_car_(United_States)#Kennedy_X-100_(1961%E2%80%931977) "Presidential state car (United States)") passed through [Dealey Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dealey_Plaza "Dealey Plaza") in Downtown Dallas.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-43) The upper two floors of the building from which the Warren Commission reported [assassin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination "Assassination")[Lee Harvey Oswald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Harvey_Oswald "Lee Harvey Oswald") shot Kennedy have been converted into a historical museum covering the former president's life and accomplishments.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-44) Kennedy was pronounced dead at Dallas [Parkland Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkland_Memorial_Hospital "Parkland Memorial Hospital") just over 30 minutes after the shooting.

On July 7, 2016, [multiple shots were fired at a Black Lives Matter protest in Downtown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_shooting_of_Dallas_police_officers "2016 shooting of Dallas police officers"), held against the police killings of two black men from other states. The gunman, later identified as Micah Xavier Johnson, began firing at police officers at 8:58 p.m., killing five officers and injuring nine. Two bystanders were also injured. This marked the deadliest day for U.S. law enforcement since the [September 11 attacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks "September 11 attacks"). Johnson told police during a standoff that he was upset about recent police shootings of black men and wanted to kill whites, especially white officers.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-45)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-46) After hours of negotiation failed, police resorted to a robot-delivered bomb, killing Johnson inside [Dallas College El Centro Campus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_College_El_Centro_Campus "Dallas College El Centro Campus"). The shooting occurred in an area of hotels, restaurants, businesses, and residential apartments only a few blocks away from Dealey Plaza.

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/The_Crescent_Uptown_Dallas.jpg/250px-The_Crescent_Uptown_Dallas.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Crescent_Uptown_Dallas.jpg)

[Uptown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Dallas "Uptown Dallas") with [Downtown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dallas "Downtown Dallas") on the end

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a3/Dallas_bridge_skyline.jpg/250px-Dallas_bridge_skyline.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dallas_bridge_skyline.jpg)

Named after a Dallas philanthropist, the [Margaret Hunt Hill Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Hunt_Hill_Bridge "Margaret Hunt Hill Bridge") spans the [Trinity River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_River_(Texas) "Trinity River (Texas)").

Dallas is situated in the [Southern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_United_States "Southern United States"), in [North Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Texas "North Texas"). It is the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Dallas County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_County,_Texas "Dallas County, Texas") and portions of the city extend into neighboring [Collin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collin_County,_Texas "Collin County, Texas"), [Denton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denton_County,_Texas "Denton County, Texas"), [Kaufman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaufman_County,_Texas "Kaufman County, Texas"), and [Rockwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwall_County,_Texas "Rockwall County, Texas") counties. Many suburbs surround Dallas; three [enclaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave "Enclave") are within the city boundaries—[Cockrell Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockrell_Hill,_Texas "Cockrell Hill, Texas"), [Highland Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highland_Park,_Texas "Highland Park, Texas"), and [University Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Park,_Texas "University Park, Texas"). According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 385.8 square miles (999.3 km 2); 340.5 square miles (881.9 km 2) of Dallas is land and 45.3 square miles (117.4 km 2) of it (11.75%) is water.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-47) Dallas makes up one-fifth of the much larger urbanized area known as the [Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_metroplex "Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex"), in which one quarter of all Texans live.

### Architecture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Architecture")]

See also: [List of Dallas Landmarks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Dallas_Landmarks "List of Dallas Landmarks") and [List of tallest buildings in Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_in_Dallas "List of tallest buildings in Dallas")

Dallas's skyline has twenty buildings classified as [skyscrapers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper "Skyscraper"), over 490 feet (150 m) in height.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-48) Despite its tallest building not reaching 980 feet (300 m), Dallas does have a signature building in [Bank of America Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America_Plaza_(Dallas) "Bank of America Plaza (Dallas)") which is lit up in neon but falls outside the top two hundred tallest buildings in the world. Although some of Dallas's architecture dates from the late 19th and early 20th centuries, most of the notable architecture in the city is from the [modernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") and [postmodernist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmodern_architecture "Postmodern architecture") eras. Iconic examples of modernist architecture include [Reunion Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reunion_Tower "Reunion Tower"), the [John Fitzgerald Kennedy Memorial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fitzgerald_Kennedy_Memorial "John Fitzgerald Kennedy Memorial"), [I. M. Pei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I._M._Pei "I. M. Pei")'s [Dallas City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_City_Hall "Dallas City Hall") and the [Morton H. Meyerson Symphony Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morton_H._Meyerson_Symphony_Center "Morton H. Meyerson Symphony Center").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-49) Good examples of postmodernist skyscrapers are [Fountain Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountain_Place "Fountain Place"), [Bank of America Plaza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_of_America_Plaza_(Dallas) "Bank of America Plaza (Dallas)"), [Renaissance Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Tower_(Dallas) "Renaissance Tower (Dallas)"), [JPMorgan Chase Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPMorgan_Chase_Tower_(Dallas) "JPMorgan Chase Tower (Dallas)"), and [Comerica Bank Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comerica_Bank_Tower "Comerica Bank Tower"). [Downtown Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dallas "Downtown Dallas") also has residential offerings in downtown, some of which are signature skyline buildings.

Several smaller structures are fashioned in the [Gothic Revival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothic_Revival_architecture "Gothic Revival architecture") style, such as the [Kirby Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirby_Building "Kirby Building"), and the [neoclassical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture "Neoclassical architecture") style, as seen in the [Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Davis_Building_(Dallas,_Texas) "Davis Building (Dallas, Texas)") and [Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilson_Building_(Dallas,_Texas) "Wilson Building (Dallas, Texas)") Buildings. One architectural "hotbed" in the city is a stretch of historic houses along [Swiss Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Avenue "Swiss Avenue"), which has all shades and variants of architecture from [Victorian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_architecture "Victorian architecture") to neoclassical.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-50) The [Dallas Downtown Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Downtown_Historic_District "Dallas Downtown Historic District") protects a cross-section of Dallas commercial architecture from the 1880s to the 1940s.

### Neighborhoods

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Neighborhoods")]

See also: [List of neighborhoods in Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_neighborhoods_in_Dallas "List of neighborhoods in Dallas")

The city of Dallas is home to many areas, neighborhoods, and communities. Dallas can be divided into several geographical areas which include larger geographical sections of territory including many subdivisions or neighborhoods, forming macroneighborhoods.

#### Central Dallas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Central Dallas")]

Central Dallas is anchored by Downtown Dallas, the center of the city, along with [Oak Lawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Lawn,_Dallas "Oak Lawn, Dallas") and [Uptown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uptown_Dallas "Uptown Dallas"), areas characterized by dense retail, restaurants, and nightlife.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-51) Downtown Dallas has a variety of named districts, including the [West End Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End,_Dallas "West End, Dallas"), the [Arts District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arts_District,_Dallas "Arts District, Dallas"), the [Main Street District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Street,_Dallas "Main Street, Dallas"), [Farmers Market District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers_Market,_Dallas "Farmers Market, Dallas"), the [City Center Business District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_Center_District,_Dallas "City Center District, Dallas"), the [Convention Center District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convention_Center_District,_Dallas "Convention Center District, Dallas"), and the [Reunion District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reunion,_Dallas "Reunion, Dallas"). This area includes Uptown, [Victory Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victory_Park,_Dallas,_Texas "Victory Park, Dallas, Texas"), Harwood, Oak Lawn, [Dallas Design District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Design_District_Dallas,_Texas "The Design District Dallas, Texas"), [Trinity Groves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_Groves,_Dallas "Trinity Groves, Dallas"), [Turtle Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_Creek,_Dallas "Turtle Creek, Dallas"), [Cityplace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cityplace,_Dallas "Cityplace, Dallas"), [Knox/Henderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knox_Park,_Dallas "Knox Park, Dallas"), [Greenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Greenville,_Dallas "Lower Greenville, Dallas"), and [West Village](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Village,_Dallas "West Village, Dallas").

#### East Dallas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: East Dallas")]

[East Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Dallas "East Dallas") is the location of [Deep Ellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_Ellum "Deep Ellum"), an arts area close to Downtown, the [Lakewood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakewood,_Dallas "Lakewood, Dallas") neighborhood (and adjacent areas, including [Lakewood Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakewood_Heights,_Dallas "Lakewood Heights, Dallas"), [Wilshire Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilshire_Heights,_Dallas "Wilshire Heights, Dallas"), [Lower Greenville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lower_Greenville,_Dallas "Lower Greenville, Dallas"), [Junius Heights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junius_Heights,_Dallas "Junius Heights, Dallas"), and [Hollywood Heights/Santa Monica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Heights,_Dallas "Hollywood Heights, Dallas")), [Vickery Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vickery_Place "Vickery Place") and [Bryan Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Place "Bryan Place"), and the architecturally significant neighborhoods of Swiss Avenue and [Munger Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munger_Place "Munger Place"). Its historic district has one of the largest collections of [Frank Lloyd Wright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lloyd_Wright "Frank Lloyd Wright")-inspired [prairie-style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Lloyd_Wright#Prairie_Style_houses_(1900%E2%80%931914) "Frank Lloyd Wright") homes in the United States. In the northeast quadrant of the city is [Lake Highlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Highlands "Lake Highlands"), one of Dallas's most unified middle-class neighborhoods.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-lhaia-52)

#### Oak Cliff

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Oak Cliff")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/44/Oak_Cliff_September_2016_51_%28Dallas_Streetcar%29.jpg/250px-Oak_Cliff_September_2016_51_%28Dallas_Streetcar%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oak_Cliff_September_2016_51_(Dallas_Streetcar).jpg)

[Oak Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Cliff "Oak Cliff") area with its [Dallas Streetcar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Streetcar "Dallas Streetcar") and Downtown Dallas on the end

Southwest of Downtown lies [Oak Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Cliff "Oak Cliff"). Once a separate city founded in the mid-1800s, Oak Cliff was annexed in 1903 by Dallas.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-53) As one of the oldest areas in Dallas, the hilly North Oak Cliff is home to 5 of the 13 conservation districts in Dallas including the architecturally significant [Kessler Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kessler,_Dallas "Kessler, Dallas") neighborhood and trendy [Bishop Arts District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_Arts_District,_Dallas "Bishop Arts District, Dallas").

#### South Dallas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dallas&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: South Dallas")]

[South Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dallas "South Dallas") is the location of [Cedars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedars,_Dallas "Cedars, Dallas"), and [Fair Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_Park "Fair Park"), where the annual [State Fair of Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Fair_of_Texas "State Fair of Texas") is held from late September through mid-October. Also located here is [Exposition Park, Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exposition_Park,_Dallas "Exposition Park, Dallas"), noted for having artists, art galleries, and bars along tree-lined Exposition Avenue.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-54)

South Side Dallas is a popular location for nightly entertainment. The neighborhood has undergone extensive development and community integration. What was once an area characterized by high rates of poverty and crime is now one of the city's most attractive social and living destinations.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-55)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-56)

Further east, in the southeast quadrant of the city, is the large neighborhood of [Pleasant Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Grove,_Dallas "Pleasant Grove, Dallas"). Once an independent city, it is a collection of mostly lower-income residential areas stretching to [Seagoville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seagoville,_Texas "Seagoville, Texas") in the southeast. Though a city neighborhood, Pleasant Grove is surrounded by undeveloped land on all sides. Swampland and wetlands separating it from South Dallas are part of the [Great Trinity Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Trinity_Forest "Great Trinity Forest"),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-The_Great_Trinity_Forest-Dallas-57) a subsection of the city's [Trinity River Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_River_Project "Trinity River Project"), newly appreciated for habitat and [flood control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flood_control "Flood control").

Main article: [Geology of the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geology_of_the_Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_Metroplex "Geology of the Dallas–Fort Worth Metroplex")

Dallas and its surrounding area are mostly flat. The city lies at elevations ranging from 450 to 550 feet (137 to 168 m) above sea level. The western edge of the Austin Chalk Formation, a [limestone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limestone "Limestone")[escarpment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escarpment "Escarpment") (also known as the "White Rock Escarpment"), rises 230 feet (70 m) and runs roughly north–south through Dallas County. South of the [Trinity River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_River_(Texas) "Trinity River (Texas)"), the uplift is particularly noticeable in the neighborhoods of Oak Cliff and the adjacent cities of Cockrell Hill, [Cedar Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_Hill,_Texas "Cedar Hill, Texas"), [Grand Prairie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Prairie,_Texas "Grand Prairie, Texas"), and [Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irving,_Texas "Irving, Texas"). Marked variations in terrain are also found in cities immediately to the west in [Tarrant County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarrant_County,_Texas "Tarrant County, Texas") surrounding Fort Worth, as well as along Turtle Creek north of Downtown.

Dallas, like many other cities, was founded along a river. The city was founded at the location of a "white rock crossing" of the Trinity River, where it was easier for wagons to cross the river in the days before ferries or bridges. The Trinity River, though not usefully navigable, is the major waterway through the city. [I-35E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_35E_(Texas) "Interstate 35E (Texas)") parallels its path through Dallas along the [Stemmons Corridor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stemmons_Corridor "Stemmons Corridor"), then south alongside the western portion of Downtown and past South Dallas and Pleasant Grove, where the river is paralleled by [Interstate 45](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_45_(Texas) "Interstate 45 (Texas)") until it exits the city and heads southeast towards [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston"). The river is flanked on both sides by 50 feet (15 m) tall earthen [levees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levee "Levee") to protect the city from frequent floods.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-58)

Since it was rerouted in the late 1920s, the river has been little more than a drainage ditch within a floodplain for several miles above and below Downtown, with a more normal course further upstream and downstream, but as Dallas began shifting towards postindustrial society, public outcry about the lack of aesthetic and recreational use of the river ultimately gave way to the [Trinity River Project](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trinity_River_Project "Trinity River Project"),[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-59) which was begun in the early 2000s.

The project area reaches for over 20 miles (32 km) in length within the city, while the overall geographical land area addressed by the Land Use Plan is approximately 44,000 acres (180 km 2) in size—about 20% of the land area in Dallas. Green space along the river encompasses approximately 10,000 acres (40 km 2), making it one of the largest and diverse urban parks in the world.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-60)

[White Rock Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Rock_Lake "White Rock Lake") and [Joe Pool Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Pool_Lake "Joe Pool Lake") are reservoirs that comprise Dallas's other significant water features. Built at the beginning of the 20th century, White Rock Lake Park is a popular destination for boaters, rowers, joggers, and bikers, as well as visitors seeking peaceful respite from the city at the 66-acre (267,000 m 2)[Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Arboretum_and_Botanical_Garden "Dallas Arboretum and Botanical Garden"), on the lake's eastern shore. [White Rock Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Rock_Creek "White Rock Creek") feeds into White Rock Lake and then exits into the Trinity River southeast of Downtown Dallas. Trails along White Rock Creek are part of the extensive Dallas County Trails System.

[Bachman Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachman_Lake "Bachman Lake"), just northwest of [Love Field Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Love_Field "Dallas Love Field"), is a smaller lake also popularly used for recreation. Northeast of the city is [Lake Ray Hubbard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Ray_Hubbard "Lake Ray Hubbard"), a vast 22,745-acre (92 km 2) reservoir in an extension of Dallas surrounded by the suburbs of [Garland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garland,_Texas "Garland, Texas"), [Rowlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rowlett,_Texas "Rowlett, Texas"), [Rockwall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rockwall,_Texas "Rockwall, Texas"), and [Sunnyvale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunnyvale,_Texas "Sunnyvale, Texas").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-61) To the west of the city is [Mountain Creek Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountain_Creek_Lake "Mountain Creek Lake"), once home to the [Naval Air Station Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Air_Station_Dallas "Naval Air Station Dallas") ([Hensley Field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hensley_Field "Hensley Field")) and a number of defense aircraft manufacturers.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-62)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-handbook-63)[North Lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Lake_(Dallas_County,_Texas) "North Lake (Dallas County, Texas)"), a small body of water in an extension of the city limits surrounded by Irving and [Coppell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coppell,_Texas "Coppell, Texas"), initially served as a water source for a nearby power plant but is now being targeted for redevelopment as a recreational lake due to its proximity to [Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas%E2%80%93Fort_Worth_International_Airport "Dallas–Fort Worth International Airport"), a plan the lake's neighboring cities oppose.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-64)

Dallas has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") ([Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"): _Cfa_, [Trewartha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trewartha_climate_classification "Trewartha climate classification"): _Cfhk_) characteristic of the [Southern Plains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Plains "Great Plains") of the United States. It also has both continental and tropical characteristics, characterized by a relatively wide annual temperature range for the latitude. Located at the lower end of [Tornado Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_Alley "Tornado Alley"), it is prone to extreme weather, tornadoes, and hailstorms.

Summers in Dallas are very hot with moderate to high humidity, although extended periods of dry weather often occur. July and August are typically the hottest months, with an average high of 96.0[°F](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fahrenheit "Fahrenheit") (36[°C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celsius "Celsius")) and an average low of 76.7°F (25°C). Heat indices regularly surpass 105°F (41°C) due to elevated humidity during the summer months, making the summer heat almost unbearable. The all-time record high is 113°F (45°C), set on June 26 and 27, 1980 during the [Heat Wave of 1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_Wave_of_1980 "Heat Wave of 1980") at nearby [Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas/Fort_Worth_International_Airport "Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-NOAA_Online-66)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-NWS_Records-67)

Winters in Dallas are usually mild, with occasional cold spells. The average date of first frost is November 12, and the average date of last frost is March 12.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-68) January is typically the coldest month, with an average daytime high of 56.8°F (14°C) and an average nighttime low of 37.3°F (3°C). The normal daily average temperature in January is 47.0°F (8°C) but sharp swings in temperature can occur, as strong cold fronts known as "[Blue Northers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Norther "Texas Norther")" pass through the Dallas region, forcing temperatures below the 40°F (4°C) mark for several days at a time and often between days with high temperatures above 80°F (27°C). Snow accumulation is seen in the city in about 70% of winter seasons, and snowfall generally occurs 1–2 days out of the year for a seasonal average of 1.5 inches (4 cm). Some areas in the region, however, receive more than that, while other areas receive negligible snowfall or none at all.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-69) The all-time record low temperature within the city is −10°F (−23°C), set on February 12, 1899, during the [Great Blizzard of 1899](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Blizzard_of_1899 "Great Blizzard of 1899").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-70) The temperature at nearby [Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas/Fort_Worth_International_Airport "Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport") reached −2°F (−19°C) on February 16, 2021, during [the February 2021 North American winter storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13%E2%80%9317,_2021_North_American_winter_storm "February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm").

Spring and autumn are transitional seasons with moderate and pleasant weather. Vibrant [wildflowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wildflower "Wildflower") (such as the [bluebonnet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluebonnet_(plant) "Bluebonnet (plant)"), [Indian paintbrush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castilleja "Castilleja") and other [flora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flora_(plants) "Flora (plants)")) bloom in spring and are planted around the highways throughout Texas.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-71) Springtime weather can be [quite volatile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Severe_weather "Severe weather"), but temperatures themselves are mild. Late spring to early summer also tends to be the most humid, with humidity levels frequently exceeding 75%. The weather in Dallas is also generally pleasant from late September to early December and on many winter days. Autumn often brings more storms and tornado threats, but they are usually fewer and less severe than in spring.

Each spring, cold fronts moving south from the North collide with warm, humid air streaming in from the [Gulf Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Coast "Gulf Coast"), leading to severe [thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorm "Thunderstorm") with [lightning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lightning "Lightning"), torrents of rain, [hail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hail "Hail"), and occasionally, [tornadoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado "Tornado"). Over time, tornadoes have probably been the most significant natural threat to the city, as it is near the heart of [Tornado Alley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_Alley "Tornado Alley").

A few times each winter in Dallas, warm and humid air from the south will override cold, dry air, resulting in [freezing rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freezing_rain "Freezing rain") or ice and causing disruptions in the city if the roads and highways become slick. Temperatures reaching 70°F (21°C) on average occur on at least four days each winter month. Dallas averages 26 annual nights at or below freezing,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-NOAA_Online-66) with the winter of 1999–2000 holding the record for the fewest freezing nights with 14. During this same span of 15 years,[_[specify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing\_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources")_] the temperature in the region has only twice dropped below 15°F (−9°C), though it will generally fall below 20°F (−7°C) in most (67%) years.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-NOAA_Online-66)

The [U.S. Department of Agriculture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USDA "USDA") places Dallas in [Plant Hardiness Zone 8b](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USDA_plant_hardiness_zone "USDA plant hardiness zone").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-72)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-73) However, mild winter temperatures in the past 15 to 20 years had encouraged the horticulture of more cold-sensitive plants such as _[Washingtonia filifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washingtonia\_filifera "Washingtonia filifera")_ and _[Washingtonia filifera var. robusta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washingtonia\_filifera\_var.\_robusta "Washingtonia filifera var. robusta")_[palms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_tree "Palm tree"), nearly all of which died off during [the February 2021 North American winter storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/February_13%E2%80%9317,_2021_North_American_winter_storm "February 13–17, 2021 North American winter storm"). According to the [American Lung Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Lung_Association "American Lung Association"), Dallas has the 12th highest air pollution among U.S. cities, ranking it behind Los Angeles and [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-74) Much of the air pollution in Dallas and the surrounding area comes from a hazardous materials incineration plant in the small town of [Midlothian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midlothian,_Texas "Midlothian, Texas") and from cement plants in neighboring [Ellis County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellis_County,_Texas "Ellis County, Texas").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-75)

The average daily low in Dallas is 57.4°F (14°C), and the average daily high is 76.9°F (25°C). Dallas receives approximately 39.1 inches (993 mm) of rain per year. The record snowfall for Dallas was 11.2 inches (28 cm) on February 11, 2010.

Dallas is the [ninth-most-populous city in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_cities_by_population "List of United States cities by population") and [third in Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Texas_by_population "List of cities in Texas by population") after the cities of [Houston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston "Houston") and [San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio "San Antonio").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Infoplease-2023-12) Its metropolitan area encompasses one-quarter of the population of Texas, and is the largest in the Southern U.S. and [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Texas_metropolitan_areas "List of Texas metropolitan areas") followed by the [Greater Houston metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Houston "Greater Houston"). At the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census") the city of Dallas had 1,304,379 residents, an increase of 106,563 since the [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_Census "2010 United States Census").[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-American_Factfinder-2020-86) However, as of July 1, 2022, the U.S. Census Bureau estimates that Dallas, in the first years since the 2020 census, lost 4,835 people, leaving the city with a population of 1,299,544.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-QuickFacts-3)

There were 524,498 households at the 2020 estimates,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2020-87) up from 2010's 458,057 households, out of which 137,523 had children under the age of 18 living with them.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2020a-88) Approximately 36.2% of households were headed by married couples living together, 57.2% had a single householder male or female with no spouse present, and 35.6% were classified as non-family households with the householder living alone.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2020-87) In 2010, 33.7% of all households had one or more people under 18 years of age, and 17.6% had one or more people who were 65 years of age or older. The average household size in 2020 was 2.52 and the average family size was 3.41.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2020a-88) In 2018, the owner-occupied housing rate was 40.2% and the renter-occupied housing rate was 59.8%.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-89) At the 2010 census, the city's age distribution of the population showed 26.5% under the age of 18 and 8.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 31.8 years. In 2010, 50.0% of the population was male and 50.0% was female.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Census_20102-90) In 2020, the median age 32.9 years; for every 100 females, there were 98.4 males.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-91)

According to the 2020 [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey"), the median income for a household in the city was $54,747; families had a median household income of $60,895; married-couple families $81,761; and non-families $45,658.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-92) In 2003–2007's survey, male full-time workers had a median income of $32,265 versus $32,402 for female full-time workers. The per capita income for the city was $25,904. About 18.7% of families and 21.7% of the population were below the poverty line, including 33.6% of those under age 18 and 13.4% of those aged 65 or over. Per 2007's survey, the median price for a house was $129,600;[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-quickfacts.census.gov2-93) by 2020, the median price for a house was valued at $252,300, with 54.4% of owner-occupied units from $50,000 to $299,999.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-94)

The 2022 [Point-In-Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point-In-Time_Count "Point-In-Time Count") Homeless Count found there were 4,410 [homeless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homelessness "Homelessness") people in Dallas.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-95)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Troisi-2022-96) According to the Metro Dallas Homeless Alliance Continuum of Care 2022 Homeless Count & Survey Independent Analysis, "approximately 1 of 3 (31%) those experiencing homelessness were found on the streets or in other places not meant for human habitation."[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-Troisi-2022-96)

The region surrounding Dallas is a habitat for mosquitoes, creating a pest problem for humans. Dallas and the surrounding area is sprayed regularly to control mosquito-borne diseases such as [West Nile virus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Nile_virus "West Nile virus").[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-97)

Dallas's population was historically predominantly White (non-Hispanic Whites made up 82.8% of the population in 1930),[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-census12-102) but its population has diversified due to immigration and [white flight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_flight "White flight") over the 20th century. Since then, the non-Hispanic White population has declined to less than one-third of the city's population.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-103) According to the 2010 U.S. census, 50.7% of the population was White (28.8% non-Hispanic White), 24.8% was Black or African American, 0.7% [American Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") and [Alaska Native](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alaska_Natives "Alaska Natives"), 2.9% Asian, and 2.6% from [two or more races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiracial_Americans "Multiracial Americans"); 42.4% of the total population was of Hispanic or Latino American origin (they may be of any race).[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-104)

At the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau")'s 2019 estimates, 29.1% were [non-Hispanic White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Hispanic_Whites "Non-Hispanic Whites") 24.3% Black and African American, 0.3% American Indian or Alaska Native, 3.7% Asian, and 1.4% from two or more races.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-105)[Native Hawaiian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Hawaiians "Native Hawaiians") and [other Pacific Islanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander") made up a total of 312 residents according to 2019's census estimates, down from 606 in 2017.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2019-106) Hispanic or Latino Americans of any race made up 41.2% of the estimated population in 2019. Among the Hispanic or Latino American population in 2019, 34.6% of Dallas was [Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Americans "Mexican Americans"), 0.4% [Puerto Rican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rican_people "Puerto Rican people"), 0.2% [Cuban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban_Americans "Cuban Americans") and 6.0% other Hispanic or Latino American. In 2017's American Community Survey estimates among the demographic 35.5% were Mexican, 0.6% Puerto Rican, 0.4% Cuban, and 5.4% other Hispanic or Latino.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-107) By 2020, Hispanic or Latino Americans of any race continued to constitute the largest ethnic group in the city proper,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-US_Census-2022-98) reflecting nationwide demographic trends.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-108)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-109)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-110)

The Dallas area is a major living destination for [Mexican Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Americans "Mexican Americans") and other Hispanic and Latino American immigrants. The southwestern portion of the city, particularly [Oak Cliff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_Cliff "Oak Cliff"), is chiefly inhabited by Hispanic and Latino American residents.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-111)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-112) The southeastern portion of the city [Pleasant Grove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleasant_Grove,_Dallas,_Texas "Pleasant Grove, Dallas, Texas") is chiefly inhabited by African American and Hispanic or Latino American residents, while the [southern portion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dallas "South Dallas") of the city is predominantly black.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-113)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-114) The west and east sides of the city are predominantly Hispanic or Latino American; [Garland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garland,_Texas "Garland, Texas") also has a large Spanish-speaking population. [North Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Dallas "North Dallas") has many enclaves of predominantly white, black and especially Hispanic or Latino American residents.

The Dallas area is also a major living destination for Black and African Americans primarily due to its strong and diverse economy.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-115)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-116) Between 2010 and 2020, the Dallas area had the second-most new Black and African American residents only behind the [Atlanta area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_metropolitan_area "Atlanta metropolitan area") and slightly above the Houston area.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-117) The notable influx of African Americans is partly due to the [New Great Migration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Great_Migration "New Great Migration").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-118) There is a significant number of people from the [Horn of Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_of_Africa "Horn of Africa"), immigrants from [Ethiopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethiopian_Americans "Ethiopian Americans"), [Eritrea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Americans "Eritrean Americans") and [Somalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somali_Americans "Somali Americans").[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-119)

The Dallas–Fort-Worth metroplex had an estimated 70,000 Russian-speakers (as of November 6, 2012) mostly immigrants from the former [Soviet Bloc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Bloc "Soviet Bloc").[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-120) Included in this population are [Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Americans "Russian Americans"), [Russian Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Jews_in_Russia "History of the Jews in Russia"), [Ukrainians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Americans "Ukrainian Americans"), [Armenians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenian_Americans "Armenian Americans"), [Belarusians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belarusian_Americans "Belarusian Americans"), [Moldavians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moldovan_Americans "Moldovan Americans")[Uzbek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbek_Americans "Uzbek Americans"), [Kirghiz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrgyz_people "Kyrgyz people"), and others. The Russian-speaking population of Dallas has continued to grow in the sector of "American husbands-Russian wives". Russian DFW has its own newspaper, _The Dallas Telegraph_.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-121)[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-122)

In addition, Dallas and its suburbs are home to a large number of Asian Americans including those of [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Americans "Indian Americans"), [Vietnamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnamese_Americans "Vietnamese Americans"), [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Americans "Chinese Americans"), [Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_Americans "Korean Americans"), [Filipino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filipino_Americans "Filipino Americans"), [Japanese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Americans "Japanese Americans"), and other heritage.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-123)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-124) Among large-sized cities in the United States, [Plano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plano,_Texas "Plano, Texas"), the northern suburb of Dallas, has the [6th largest Chinese American population](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._cities_with_significant_Chinese-American_populations#Large-sized_cities "List of U.S. cities with significant Chinese-American populations") as of 2016. The Plano-Richardson area in particular had an estimated 30,000 [Iranian Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iranian_Americans "Iranian Americans") in 2012.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-125)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-126) With so many immigrant groups, there are often multilingual signs in the [linguistic landscape](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linguistic_landscape "Linguistic landscape"). According to U.S. Census Bureau data released in December 2013, 23 percent of Dallas County residents were foreign-born, while 16 percent of Tarrant County residents were foreign-born.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-127) The 2018 census estimates determined that the city of Dallas's foreign-born population consisted of 25.4% naturalized citizens and 74.6% non-citizens.[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas#cite_note-128)
